honestyRule: A record may only carry class ANSWERS when a real measured round trip through the deployed service returned HTTP 200 with real answer text. Every other class means exactly what its name says. CONTENDED-TIMEOUT is a measurement of the POOL, not of the model. UNMEASURED means no class about the model was established. Nothing in this file is an inference, a projection, or a claim about a model that was not measured. A class is defined by the ACTION it licenses, which is why WALL-CHALLENGE (wigolo tier / honest refusal) and COMPOSER-DRIFT (selector retune) are separate members: the same HTTP 502 at the same idle pool with the same 'no composer found' message can require opposite responses, and one class would license the wrong one. The rule that draws the line is CODE, src/prompt/verification-class.ts, not a sweep convention.

poolPacing.why: The operator's standing rule is that a challenge on a real logged-in account is the one failure this project cannot recover from, so the sweep was run STRICTLY SERIALLY: one model at a time, no concurrent fan-out, and the driver waited for pool busy==0 && queued==0 before issuing each request.
poolPacing.whatWasObserved: The fixed service still leaves 1-3 workers busy for up to ~225s after a 60s per-site sign-in timeout (busyWatchdogMs=225000), which is how three models (hunyuan, inner-ai, v0) first hit pool 4/4 and timed out. Each of those three was then RE-PROBED at an idle pool and all three returned a named 502. That is a residual leak, not the old 4.77h wedge: the pool returned to idle by itself every time.
poolPacing.residualLeakHonest: This record does NOT claim the pool leak is fixed. It claims only that the pool drained within the watchdog window on every observed occasion, so contention could be told apart from model failure by re-probing at idle.

classVocabularyGap.theProblem: The gate's closed class set was {ANSWERS, SIGN-OUT, CONTENDED-TIMEOUT, UNMEASURED}. The 2026-09-30 sweep produced a real, named, per-model outcome that NO member of that set means: HTTP 502 at an IDLE pool whose own message is 'no composer found on <site> - the site UI may have changed', with the server itself reporting the page title/url it landed on. That is a distinct condition from a sign-in (the message does not say sign-in, and some of those pages are not login pages at all - one is a Cloudflare 'Attention Required!' challenge and one is a Vercel Security Checkpoint).
classVocabularyGap.whatWasRefused: Filing these as SIGN-OUT would overstate (it asserts a credential problem the evidence does not show). Filing them as CONTENDED-TIMEOUT would be a lie and the gate itself rejects it at an idle pool (RULE 7).
classVocabularyGap.whatWasDoneInsteadOn2026-09-30: They were filed UNMEASURED - read strictly as 'no ANSWERS class and no SIGN-OUT class was established for this run' - while the REAL measurement was carried in measuredAt/method/evidence/prereq. That was true and it under-reported what the sweep had established.
classVocabularyGap.howItWasClosedOn2026-09-30ByGOAL158: The set gained two members THAT DAY - WALL-CHALLENGE and COMPOSER-DRIFT - and the rule that fills them became code (see classificationRule). The 7 rows are re-filed, with the server-reported page title+url now machine-readable in observedPage rather than buried in a prose evidence string. NOTHING WAS RE-MEASURED: every row keeps its measured HTTP status, its measuredAt, its poolAtRequest, and its evidence string verbatim. Only the class changed, and only because a class for the observed condition now exists. THE VOCABULARY HAS SINCE GROWN AGAIN, so 'two' is the count for 2026-09-30 and NOT the count now: measured against the original four (ANSWERS, SIGN-OUT, CONTENDED-TIMEOUT, UNMEASURED) the set has gained FIVE members, not two - WALL-CHALLENGE and COMPOSER-DRIFT here, plus NON-ANSWER-READ, ANSWER-UNREADABLE and UNATTRIBUTED-NO-ANSWER, which arrived on later measurements and carry the v0 and venice rows this re-filing had no class for. classes.ANSWERS: a real measured round trip returned HTTP 200 with real answer text from the model's own site, at an idle pool
classes.SIGN-OUT: the server returned a NAMED 502 whose own message says sign-in is required, OR whose own reported page title/url IS a login/sign-in page (deepseek /sign_in, claude 'Sign in - Claude', huggingchat /login?next=, poe /login?redirect_url=)
classes.CONTENDED-TIMEOUT: a request was issued and got no response (HTTP 000, client abort) while the pool was NOT idle — a measurement of queue contention, NOT a property of the model
classes.UNMEASURED: never reached. NOTHING was measured, so nothing may be claimed - in particular the evidence field must not quote a measured HTTP status (RULE 9), because a real response WAS reached on any row that has one. As of 2026-09-30 zero rows carry this class: the 9 that were UNMEASURED-for-lack-of-reach on 2026-09-29 were all reached, and the 7 that were UNMEASURED-by-omission on 2026-09-30 were re-filed into WALL-CHALLENGE (3) and COMPOSER-DRIFT (4).
classes.WALL-CHALLENGE: the server landed on an ANTI-BOT INTERSTITIAL and reported it: HTTP 502 at an IDLE pool whose own message is 'no composer found on <site> - the site UI may have changed', with the server-reported page title/url matching a challenge marker (Cloudflare 'Attention Required!' / 'Just a moment...', Vercel Security Checkpoint). The named action is the wigolo tier per docs/WIGOLO_BYPASS.md, or an honest ok:false - NEVER a retry loop, because a challenge on a real logged-in account is the one failure this project cannot recover from. Requires measuredAt + method + evidence + observedPage and an IDLE pool.
classes.COMPOSER-DRIFT: the page LOADED and is neither a sign-in surface nor a challenge, but the composer selector found nothing: HTTP 502 at an IDLE pool, 'no composer found on <site> - the site UI may have changed', and the server-reported page title/url is a real product surface (or, for notion, the public marketing landing page the redirect landed on). The session is fine; the selectors are stale. The named action is a profile/selector retune, NOT a login. Requires measuredAt + method + evidence + observedPage and an IDLE pool.
classes.NON-ANSWER-READ: a 2xx arrived at an IDLE pool carrying text that is NOT the model's answer: the read SUCCEEDED and the text was still not an answer, because the answer selector resolved inside a region the site itself marks as activity/status. This is the only class in the set keyed on a 2xx, and it is the sharpest hazard here precisely because it arrives looking like success - a 200 is not evidence of an answer. Measured on v0 2026-09-30 (HTTP 200 in 13543ms carrying 'Exploring ideas...', v0's agent-activity placeholder). It is NOT ANSWERS, and it is NOT COMPOSER-DRIFT, because the selector found the WRONG node rather than no node. The named action is a profile/selector retune that declares the region a non-answer, never a promotion. Requires measuredAt + method + evidence and an IDLE pool.
classes.ANSWER-UNREADABLE: the profile's answer selector matched NOTHING in the page's real DOM, at an IDLE pool, so no answer was obtainable. THIS DOES NOT MEAN THE MODEL FAILED TO ANSWER: the row's meaning is 'the DRIVER cannot read this model', not 'this model cannot answer'. Measured on venice 2026-09-30, where a read-only CDP inspection of the tab the driver left behind showed venice's answer was 'PONG' in that very DOM while the GOAL-160 selectors matched zero nodes - so the earlier 'paraphrases instead of complying' finding was an ARTEFACT OF THE PROFILE. It is not a credential problem and not an anti-bot wall, and it is not COMPOSER-DRIFT (that is a missing composer; this is a missing ANSWER). The named action is a profile/selector retune DERIVED FROM A CAPTURE, never a guess from a failure - deriving selectors from a failure is what produced this condition. Requires measuredAt + method + evidence and an IDLE pool.
classes.UNATTRIBUTED-NO-ANSWER: a no-answer the service reported and COULD NOT ATTRIBUTE: the service's own named refusal sentence ("did not return an answer within <n>ms") arrived at an IDLE pool carrying no observedPage, no anti-bot page, no credential requirement named in the message, and no missing composer - so WHAT IS KNOWN is that there was no answer, while WHICH CAUSE produced it is UNKNOWN. The refusal LISTS its candidates (the site may be busy, may be rate-limiting, may be showing a sign-in or consent wall) and asserts NONE of them, and this measurement cannot tell them apart, so the class must never be read as "the site is rate-limited" or "log in" or "the model is broken": four identical measurements do not single out one of three candidates the service itself named, and this record's own history holds the precedent (a busy-pool timeout filed as a model property produced a 4.77-hour diagnosis that was wrong). The action it licenses is RE-MEASURE WITH A DISCRIMINATOR that separates the candidates, never an assumed remedy. Measured on v0 2026-09-30 (four identical 502s at an idle pool, 97195ms / 96440ms / 96440ms). It is NOT CONTENDED-TIMEOUT (that is a queue property and the pool was idle), NOT SIGN-OUT (the message names no credential requirement) and NOT COMPOSER-DRIFT (the composer resolved and the request was sent). Requires measuredAt + method + an evidence string carrying the refusal sentence, plus poolAtRequest and an IDLE pool; it deliberately does NOT require observedPage, because the service reported no page on this path.

control.whyItMatters: duckduckgo is THE FALSIFIER for this sweep. It is the same model that the 2026-09-29 sweep recorded as CONTENDED-TIMEOUT (HTTP 000 after 200009ms at pool 3/4) even though it had answered minutes earlier. It was probed FIRST this run, before any other model, and it answered 200 with a real PONG in 9201ms at an idle pool. It was probed AGAIN LAST, after 20 other models had each driven a real browser, and it answered 200 again in 10049ms at an idle pool. So: (a) a model that answers can time out in this service, which is what makes CONTENDED-TIMEOUT a queue property rather than a model property; (b) the service was alive at the start AND the end of the sweep, so every non-answer between those two points is attributable to the model, not to the service dying.

records.evidence: FIXED CLASS, NOT A DIAGNOSIS OF WHICH CAUSE. THE MEASUREMENT IS UNCHANGED (deployed build 5168940): POST /v1/chat/completions {model:v0, prompt 'Reply with exactly: PONG'} returned HTTP 502 FOUR times, serially, every one at an IDLE pool (busy 0, queued 0), every one carrying the SAME service refusal "v0 did not return an answer within 90000ms - the site may be busy, rate-limiting, or showing a sign-in or consent wall. Retry; if it repeats, pick another model id from GET /v1/models." Measured 97195ms, 96440ms and 96440ms on the three retained attempts. WHAT THE SERVICE NAMED, AND WHAT IT DID NOT ASSERT: that sentence LISTS three candidate causes - the site may be busy, may be rate-limiting, or may be showing a wall - and asserts NONE of them. Four identical measurements therefore CANNOT TELL THE CANDIDATES APART. WHAT IS KNOWN: a no-answer was reported, at an IDLE pool, with no page reported, no anti-bot marker on any page, no credential requirement named in the message, the composer resolved and the request was sent. WHICH CAUSE PRODUCED IT IS NOT KNOWN. THIS CLASS RECORDS THAT AND NOTHING MORE: 'v0 is rate-limited' would be a fabrication, because four identical refusals cannot single out one of the three candidates the service itself named - and this project's own record holds the exact precedent, a busy-pool timeout filed as a model property which produced a 4.77-hour diagnosis that turned out to be wrong. THE ACTION THIS CLASS LICENSES IS RE-MEASURE WITH A DISCRIMINATOR that separates the candidates the service named, never a retry loop and never an assumed remedy. WHAT CHANGED FOR THE BETTER: the 200-with-'Exploring ideas...' non-answer that GOAL 160 was written to kill is GONE - the status region was not served as the answer on any attempt - though that is NOT proof the GOAL-163 fix works, because the read no longer reaches the point where it could serve the placeholder, so the fix remains a BUNDLE HYPOTHESIS. NOT PROMOTED: v0 never returned an answer, so this row is not ANSWERS, and the pool was idle so it is not CONTENDED-TIMEOUT either. THE DOM CAPTURE FAILED AGAIN, AND THE CAUSE IS DIFFERENT AND WORSE THAN LAST TIME - NAMED PLAINLY: last time the capture attached to a stale landing-page tab; this time there was NO v0 tab AT ALL to attach to. GET /status reported the v0 pool worker healthy and idle ('health': 'live', busy false) throughout, but a read-only CDP enumeration of the daemon's own Chrome (127.0.0.1:9222, pid 3376878, --user-data-dir /home/ui2api/.config/ui2api-chrome) listed 17 targets and NOT ONE was v0.app - the pool's page is not visible to CDP at all. A poller sampling every 6s for 110s CONCURRENT WITH a live v0 request captured ZERO v0 snapshots. So the driven /chat tab remains unreachable read-only, which is precisely the discriminator this row's next action requires, and NO SELECTOR WAS CHANGED - a profile edit made to make a measurement pass is exactly the failure this record exists to catch. NARRATION DISCIPLINE, KEPT: the four phrases this classifier keys on for the credential condition are described here by paraphrase and never quoted, because RULE 11 feeds this whole evidence string to the classifier, and an earlier version of this paragraph quoted one of them inside a sentence DENYING it - the row was reading its own refutation as a match. Only that self-match was removed; the measurement never changed. RE-DERIVED 2026-09-30 (GOAL 168), NOT HAND-FILED: classifyOutcome() was run over this row's own httpStatus/evidence/poolAtRequest and derives UNATTRIBUTED-NO-ANSWER, because the service's own refusal sentence matches its marker and nothing more specific matched first. RULE 11 re-derives every measured row, so a hand-filed class here would be caught.

records.evidence: UNCLASSIFIED - AND THE CLASSIFIER WOULD FILE IT AS ANSWERS, WHICH WOULD BE A FABRICATION. MEASUREMENT: POST /v1/chat/completions {model:venice, prompt 'Reply with exactly: PONG'} -> HTTP 200 in 41793ms at pool busy 0 / total 3 / queued 0 (IDLE), on its FIRST attempt (no retry used). Body answer text, the server's own: 'The user wants me to reply with exactly "PONG". This is a simple request - I should just output the text "P..."' - the model's reasoning narrating the instruction, NOT the requested token. THE SELECTOR IS CONFIRMED GOOD, MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE DOM. A read-only CDP capture (Runtime.evaluate only; no navigation, no typing, no request to the site) of the venice tab shows 'div[class~="assistant"] [class*="prose"]' matching EXACTLY ONE node, cls 'space-y-4 whitespace-normal [&>*:first-child]:mt-0 [&>*:last-child]:mb-0 prose dark:prose-invert flex-1', text 'PONG'; the page body reads 'Use Classic Chat / Reply with exactly: PONG / Worked for < 1s . 1 step / PONG'. It correctly EXCLUDES the user bubble (that one is the OTHER of the two [class*="prose"] nodes on the page, text 'Reply with exactly: PONG') and the assistant footer, and both superseded GOAL-160 selectors match ZERO nodes ([data-message-author-role="assistant"] -> 0, [class*="message"] [class*="prose"] -> 0). So GOAL 163's venice fix is CORRECT and is now confirmed against the live DOM - a real upgrade over 'unverified-selector': it reads the right node. BUT THE SERVED TEXT IS NOT IN THAT DOM. The reasoning string the service returned appears NOWHERE in the captured page body, which still holds the final 'PONG'. So the 200 served the model's INTERMEDIATE reasoning while the read settled, not the final answer. NO SELECTOR WAS CHANGED. There is no capture-derived diagnosis of WHICH node carried the reasoning - every declared nonAnswerSelector ([class*="reasoning"], [class*="thinking"], [class*="chain-of-thought"], [data-message-author-role="user"], [class*="user-message"]) matches ZERO nodes on this page, so nothing is available to declare, and widening the answer selector until the string matches would be exactly the failure this goal exists to catch. RE-DERIVED 2026-09-30 (GOAL 167), NOT HAND-FILED: classifyOutcome() was run over this row's own httpStatus/evidence/poolAtRequest and derives NON-ANSWER-READ - a 200 at an IDLE pool whose served text the record states is NOT the requested token. That class's claim is true of this measurement (the read returned a node, and what it returned was the model's intermediate reasoning), so the row carries it and RULE 4 no longer names this row. TWO THINGS A READER MUST NOT MISTAKE FOR FIXES. (1) The remedy NON-ANSWER-READ names - find which node the site served that text from and retune the profile against a capture - is NOT the confirmed remedy here: the selector is already confirmed correct against the live DOM, so the open defect is a STREAMING READ (the read settled on intermediate reasoning while the final answer was still arriving), and no selector change is licensed by this row. (2) It matched because this evidence string contains the marker phrase 'NOT the requested token'; the four NON_ANSWER_TEXT_PATTERNS are matched against the record's own evidence, so a row whose NARRATIVE quotes a marker phrase derives NON-ANSWER-READ even when the service emitted nothing of the sort. That is a property of RULE 11's feed, not a claim that the service phrased it that way. WIDENING THOSE PATTERNS to catch reasoning prose was deliberately NOT done: a regex guessing at English reasoning prose is what this record forbids.

goal163VocabularyGap.theProblem: THE CLOSED CLASS SET HAS NO MEMBER FOR THE ONE CONDITION THIS GOAL MEASURED. A row may not honestly file 'HTTP 200 carrying a non-answer' (v0) and may not honestly file 'the site answered, the profile read nothing' (venice), and every class that WOULD pass the gate is a lie: ANSWERS asserts the model answers when it served a status line; SIGN-OUT asserts a credential problem the evidence does not show; UNMEASURED is blocked by RULE 9 because a real response WAS reached; CONTENDED-TIMEOUT is blocked by RULE 7 because both rows were measured at an IDLE pool; and COMPOSER-DRIFT/WALL-CHALLENGE, the two classes whose ACTION is the retune that was actually performed, both REQUIRE an observedPage that the server never reported for either failure path.
goal163VocabularyGap.whatWasDoneInstead: Both rows are filed UNCLASSIFIED — the classifier's OWN refusal token (exported as the Unclassified type in src/prompt/verification-class.ts, and named in that module's own header as the honest state: 'a measured response that matches nothing is UNCLASSIFIED, which is not a class and is a GATE FAILURE — the honest move is to widen the rule on purpose, not to let the row hide'). RULE 4 therefore goes RED, naming exactly these two rows. That red is the DELIVERABLE, not a defect to be silenced: it is the measured proof that the vocabulary is one condition behind its own evidence, which is the identical shape of the bug GOAL 157 and GOAL 160 were each written about.

goal164Resolution.theAskAnswered: On (1), 'the selector found the wrong node' and 'the selector found nothing' are NOT one class, and the answer is a new member rather than a relaxation of COMPOSER-DRIFT. Relaxing COMPOSER-DRIFT would also have required an observedPage the server never reported on either path, so the relaxation would have been unreachable rather than stricter. On (2), an answer-side failure path may NOT report observedPage, and the new classes deliberately do not require one - requiring it would have made them unfillable and quietly pushed the rows back to UNCLASSIFIED.
